title: MERL Manager (Monitoring, Evaluation, Research & Learning)
overview: We are seeking a dynamic and skilled MERL Manager to lead the design, implementation, and oversight of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) for our programs. You will be instrumental in ensuring data driven decision-making, program accountability, and serve as the single source of verified and up-to-date program data for internal decision-making and external communication with stakeholders.continuous learning across TracTrac MSL's impactful interventions.

responsibilities.title: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)
items: Design and implement M&E frameworks for projects, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
Develop and maintain data collection tools, systems, and databases. (GIS & MIS)
Monitor project activities, collect data, and analyze results to assess progress and performance against targets.
Conduct regular field visits to gather data and provide on-the-ground support to project teams.
Prepare high-quality M&E reports for internal and external stakeholders.

responsibilities.title: Research
items: Conduct research studies, including baseline and endline surveys, impact assessments, and market research.
Analyze and interpret research findings to inform program design and decision-making.
Stay up-to-date with industry trends and best practices in MERL and incorporate relevant innovations into our programs.

responsibilities.title: Learning and Capacity Building
items: Facilitate regular learning sessions and knowledge-sharing events within the organization.
Collaborate with project teams to identify areas for improvement and adapt program strategies accordingly.
Provide training and capacity-building support to staff and partners on MERL best practices.

responsibilities.title: Data Management
items: Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and security of project data.
Develop and manage data storage and archiving systems.
Support data quality assurance efforts, including data cleaning and validation.

responsibilities.title: Partnerships & Stakeholder Engagement
items: Collaborate with partners, including government agencies and policy bodies, to align M&E activities.
Support consortium partners in adopting strong M&E systems.
Engage stakeholders in knowledge-sharing and evidence-based dialogue.

responsibilities.title: Capacity Building & Team Leadership
items: Lead and mentor MERL officers, field staff, and enumerators.
Deliver training on M&E frameworks, tools, and methodologies.
Cultivate a culture of evidence-based decision-making and learning.

responsibilities.title: General Technical Support
items: Assist the Team Leader with coordination, quality assurance, and stakeholder management.
Oversee technical aspects and deliverables of the MERL components of projects.

responsibilities.title: Reporting and Communication
items: Prepare and present MERL findings to internal and external stakeholders.
Contribute to the development of communication materials, case studies, and success stories.

qualifications: Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., social sciences, international development, statistics, or a related discipline). An advanced degree is an added advantage.
Proven experience in monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning in the development or humanitarian sector.
Strong data analysis skills and proficiency in data analysis software (e.g., Excel, SPSS, STATA, or R).
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience with quantitative and qualitative data collection methods.
Strong project management skills and attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Knowledge of relevant industry standards and best practices in MERL.

title: Content Writer & Storyteller
summary: Develop clear, compelling narratives that communicate impact, learning, and value across multiple audiences.
overview: The Content Writer & Storyteller is responsible for developing clear, compelling narratives that communicate impact, learning, and value across multiple audiences. The role involves researching stories, producing high-quality written content, supporting multimedia storytelling, and translating complex information into accessible, engaging narratives. The scope of responsibility will vary based on experience, with junior candidates receiving more guidance and mid-level candidates working more independently.

responsibilities.title: Story Development & Content Creation
items: Identify, research, and develop strong story ideas aligned with organisational priorities.
Write short- and long-form content including features, success stories, reflections, and case studies.
Maintain a steady pipeline of publishable stories.
Translate technical or operational information into clear, engaging language for diverse audiences.

responsibilities.title: Editorial & Quality Assurance
items: Produce publication-ready drafts that meet editorial standards.
Support editing, proofreading, and content refinement processes.
Incorporate feedback to improve storytelling quality and clarity.

responsibilities.title: Multimedia & Visual Storytelling Support
items: Support the development of scripts, interview guides, storyboards, and shot lists for video and multimedia content.
Collaborate with multimedia and creative teams during production and post-production.

responsibilities.title: Learning, Impact & Stakeholder Storytelling
items: Contribute to learning briefs, reports, and knowledge products.
Support the development of impact stories for partners, donors, policymakers, and public audiences.
Provide storytelling inputs for reports, proposals, and advocacy materials.

responsibilities.title: Field Engagement & Ethical Storytelling
items: Conduct interviews with internal and external stakeholders, including beneficiaries and partners.
Ensure ethical storytelling practices, including informed consent and respectful representation.
Maintain organised story notes, sources, and documentation.

responsibilities.title: Collaboration & Growth
items: Work closely with communications, program, and creative teams.
For mid-level candidates, provide light editorial support or guidance to junior writers when required.

qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, English, Marketing, or a related field.
1–3 years of experience in producing high-quality content or storytelling outputs, writing, content creation, journalism, or communications.
Strong writing and storytelling skills, with the ability to adapt tone for different audiences.
Experience translating complex or technical information into accessible narratives.
Experience working with multimedia teams is an advantage.
skills: Excellent writing and narrative development skills
Attention to detail and editorial judgment
Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines
